tools.name: check_a_no
tools.description:
Searches for things that an answer said do not exist or cannot be done:
products, apps, services, competitors, ways to do something (guides,
workarounds, open-source fixes, procedures), or evidence about a factual "no"
("no study shows...", "that's not allowed", "you're not entitled to...").

Suited to questions such as "is there an app / tool / service that...",
"are there competitors to...", "is there a way to...", "does X exist in
my country / in my language / on Shopify", or a factual or rights question whose
answer is "no".

It runs the given queries in parallel on the general web and, optionally,
inside specific places: app stores (Apple App Store, Google Play, Chrome Web
Store), plugin marketplaces (Shopify, WordPress), launch and startup sites
(Product Hunt and others), social and business pages (LinkedIn, Facebook,
Instagram), how-to sites and forums (Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, Stack Exchange,
local-language forums), and facts / research / rights sources (Wikipedia,
PubMed, arXiv, government and rights sites).

Parameters:
- claim: the "no" being checked.
- product_shape: what the product or method would do, for whom, through which
  channel or device.
- queries: 4-20 varied queries (synonyms, functional descriptions,
  "alternatives to X", "how to X", "X workaround"), in English and the user's
  language.
- marketplace_queries: 3-5 short keyword phrases (2-5 words, English) run
  inside each chosen place, e.g. "memoir WhatsApp bot".
- places: only the places that fit the question (apps/tools -> app_stores,
  plugin_marketplaces, launch_and_startup_sites, social_and_business_pages;
  "how to" -> how_to_and_forums; laws, rights, research ->
  facts_research_and_rights). Fewer places is faster and cheaper.

Returns deduplicated results (title, URL, snippet, where found) and a coverage
report: queries run, places searched and skipped, hits per place. A result
has not been verified; "not found" in these places is not proof that
something does not exist.

claim.description: What the user is asking about or the claim being checked, e.g. 'There is no service that turns seniors' voice recordings into a memoir book'.
claim.title: Claim

product_shape.description: What the product or way would do or achieve, for whom, through which channel or device. Used to judge closeness.
product_shape.title: Product Shape

queries.description: 8-20 varied search queries in English and the local language: synonyms, functional descriptions, brand-style names, 'alternatives to X', 'how to X', 'X workaround'.
queries.title: Queries

marketplace_queries.description: 3-5 SHORT keyword queries (2-5 words, English) naming the product type as a store listing would, e.g. 'sycophancy ChatGPT extension'. Run inside every app store, launch site, social site and plugin marketplace.
marketplace_queries.title: Marketplace Queries

places.description: Which special places to search besides the general web. Pick only the ones that fit the question (apps/tools -> app_stores, plugin_marketplaces, launch_and_startup_sites, social_and_business_pages; 'can I / how to' -> how_to_and_forums; laws, rights, research, history -> facts_research_and_rights). Omit to search all of them.
places.title: Places
